_comment: A broken deep cavalry block rounds a hill in its line of flight as one body. Team 1's 80 horses (default Cavalry geometry: 9 files by 9 ranks, about 320 wu wide and 960 wu deep) spawn ALREADY routing (starting_state 3, morale 1.0) facing south, their own back edge, with their front rank 40 wu short of a hill (block terrain, x 780-1040, y 1220-1420) that stands across the eastern half of the block; the block's centre line (x 820) passes 40 wu inside the hill's west face. The flight rounds the hill by its west end with the block's own half-width as its margin, so the eastern files clear the hill too, and the men whose run would still carry them onto it veer along its face instead. Before the fix the flight cleared only the anchor's own margin (a body radius plus 18 wu): the eastern files ran into the hill's north face and were held there (12 men within a wu of the face by tick 350) while the block ran on and stretched. Measured with state dumps at the declared ticks: the anchor is at about (718, 875) at tick 240 and (611, 1054) at tick 330; before the fix (788.6, 909.2) and (756.5, 1094.2). At ticks 150-180 two front-rank men brush along the hill's north face and off its western corner, moving at the block's own (still building) pace. A routing unit's rout timer (6 s) runs out at tick 360 and it rallies; the clip ends at tick 352, just before that, so it shows only the flight. A small idle team-0 squadron 600 wu east keeps the router in the close sim tier (an isolated block drops to the far tier, which has no bodies); all_teams_control leaves both sides without AI, so neither moves on its own. Flat declared map apart from the hill; drill mode. Driven live through the real SelectionManager by tools/demo/DemoInputRecorder.gd; world coordinates; physics ticks (60/s).
